newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends firm on commercial demand, China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends firm on commercial demand, China.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed higher on commercial buying which led to talk China was seeking U.S. soyoil, traders said.

After the close, it was confirmed by U.S. exporters that China bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for shipment next week and one exporter noted there was talk China's purchases Thursday may have totaled 70,000 tonnes.
Produce Grain bought 500 lots of December soyoil, traders said, and Cargill Inc sold 800 lots of December.
Unwinding of meal/oil spreads also boosted soyoil at the expense of soymeal.
New contract lows were set in the deferred months of meal with the new low for March at $220.30 per ton, down from the previous low of $222.0 which was set Monday.
Talk China has cancelled soymeal export orders from the U.S. also weighed on soymeal futures, the traders said.
Asian trading sources said Thursday that casualties are starting to mount as Chinese buyers of soybeans and soymeal default or cancel contracts in the wake of falling international prices.
Soyoil closed 0.15 to 0.35 cent per lb higher, with October up 0.27 at 22.90.
Soymeal closed $0.50 per ton higher to $4.60 lower, with October up $0.50 at $236.80. December was down $2.70 at $227.40.
